newsitem.title: GERMANY: German air safety crackdown pinpoints unsafe carriers.
newsitem.headline: German air safety crackdown pinpoints unsafe carriers.

text.p: Several foreign airlines have stopped flying to Germany following a safety crackdown by air authorities, the country's transport ministry said.
The airlines, which were not named, were "particularly unsafe" and no longer tried to apply for landing licences in Germany, a ministry statement said.
One airline, Turkish charter airline Holiday Air, had its licence withdrawn since the start of the safety crackdown last May, a ministry spokeswoman added.
The tougher safety checks were introduced after the crash of a Birgen Air aircraft off the Dominican Republic last February in which 189 people, mostly Germany tourists, died.
The German federal aviation office, the Luftfahrtbundesamt, had checked 94 additional aircraft since a new safety task force was installed last July, the ministry said.
In 23 aircraft serious defects were found, in 46 cases smaller problems not affecting safety were discovered and 25 aircraft were given the all-clear.
In addition, the German travel industry has renewed its pledge to boycott carriers not meeting German and European safety levels, the ministry said.
The voluntary ban has been agreed by airlines including Deutsche Lufthansa AG, large tour operators such as TUI and NUR and the German travel agents association DRV.
Only German airlines or carriers registered under the strict European Joint Aviation Authorities (JAA) regulations would be used by the travel industry for holiday flights and sub-charter operations.
Transport minister Matthias Wissmann said both the travel industry and public authorities agreed at a meeting that the safety measures were working well to improve air travel quality.

Foreign airlines checked in Germany were now demanding improved observance of international safety standards in their home countries in order to avoid delays in Germany, he noted. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
